sentences.text: Aegialornis was a prehistoric bird closely resembling modern treeswifts.
These creatures possessed sickle-shaped wings similar to those seen in swifts today.
Richard Lydekker first described this genus in 1891.
Fossils have been found in Middle to Late Eocene deposits across Germany and France.
The species formed a distinct family known as the Aegialornithidae.
Aegialornis is not considered a direct ancestor of modern swifts but represents a group that retained basal morphology.
It remains uncertain which other genera should be included in the family Aegialornithidae.
Remains of these birds date from the Early to Late Eocene epoch.
Scientists estimate their time range falls between 41.03 and 37.71 million years ago.
It is debated whether an Early Eocene record from the Nanjemoy Formation in Virginia belongs to Aegialornis, as apodiform birds may not have existed there until after the Eocene.
The taxonomy of Aegialornis species is debated, with some researchers considering A. germanicus and A. leenhardti as junior synonyms of A. gallicus.
It is debated whether A. broweri is based on small individuals of A. wetmorei, and the proposal to separate them into the genus Mesogiornis has not found general acceptance.
The classification of Cypselavus is debated, with it being considered either an aegialornithid or a treeswift.
The inclusion of the Jungornithidae family in the Aegialornithidae is controversial.
